therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: estrogen receptor-driven tumor cell proliferation suppression
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: ER+/HER2- advanced breast cancer patients with prior endocrine therapy and CDK4/6 inhibitor treatment
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Progression-free survival in ESR1-mutant participants and all participants

results.target_engagement_evidence: ESR1-mutant subgroup showed greater benefit (HR 0.546) vs overall population (HR 0.697), consistent with on-target activity against ESR1 mutations
biomarker_changes: ESR1 mutation status associated with differential PFS benefit: HR 0.546 in ESR1-mut vs HR 0.697 in all participants
subgroup_findings: ESR1-mutant participants: median PFS 3.78 months (elacestrant) vs 1.87 months (SoC), HR 0.546, p=0.0005
All participants: median PFS 2.79 months (elacestrant) vs 1.91 months (SoC), HR 0.697, p=0.0018
ESR1-mut OS: HR 0.592, p=0.0325 (elacestrant median OS not reached vs 16.95 months SoC)
All participants OS: HR 0.742, p=0.0697 (both medians not reached)
safety_signals: Nausea was the most common serious AE in elacestrant arm (3/237)
Vomiting and small intestinal obstruction each occurred in 2/237 elacestrant patients
Abdominal pain occurred in 2/230 SoC patients as serious AE

context.comparator: Standard of care (fulvestrant, anastrozole, letrozole, or exemestane)
